pool.text: Alfonso VI seized Madrid to use as an outpost against Toledo
Philip II moved his court to Madrid, making it the capital
Bourbon forces retook Madrid from allied Austriacist army
Reglamento General de Postas created a radial road system across Spain.
Esquilache Riots protested clothing decree in Madrid
Bank of San Carlos founded, later becoming the Bank of Spain
Las Ventas bullring, the largest in Spain, was established in Madrid.
Real Madrid Baloncesto basketball club was founded, playing at WiZink Center.
Madrid became a Republican stronghold during the Civil War
Francoist forces captured Madrid in March
EFE news agency headquartered in Madrid since its inception
Club Baloncesto Estudiantes was founded, later sharing the WiZink Center arena.
Europa Press news agency founded and headquartered in Madrid
Edificio España presented as Europe's tallest building at inauguration
Madrid's Pride Parade began in the Chueca neighbourhood, sparking LGBT rights movement.
New constitution confirmed Madrid as Spain's capital after Franco
First democratically elected mayor since Second Republic took office
Mass demonstrations supported democracy after failed coup on 23 February
Madrid announced a plan to phase out diesel vehicles within the next decade.
Film and TV industry employs 19,000 people locally
